report:
Summary finding
- The evidence supports a difference in topical/style bias: checkpoint B (the difference is B minus A) pushes activations toward tokens typical of online news/blog/social-media/ad-style text (tokens like "blog", "blogs", "blogger", "blogging", "facebook", "photo", "sexy", "ad", "ads", "Mail", "TV", month abbreviations, and many news-y/celebrity/political nouns such as "Obama", "billionaire", "politicians", "activists", "journalists", "chairman", "metropolitan", "seminar(s)").
- This difference is concentrated at the earliest token positions (pos0 and pos1 across many late layers), so it affects how sequences are started / initial token preferences (and also shows up through middle positions for the “blog”-related tokens).

Why I conclude this
- The logit-lens readouts for the highest-norm cells repeatedly point to the same family of tokens across many layers and positions: "blog", "blogs", "blogger", "blogging", "photo", "facebook", "ad"/"ads", "Mail", "TV", "sexy", and political/press words like "Obama", "billionaire", "politicians", "journalists", etc. That consistent token-level pattern implies a coherent domain/style shift rather than random noise.
- The L2 norms are very large at pos0/pos1 in many late layers (especially layers ~20–25), indicating the difference primarily modulates early-sequence residuals — consistent with a change in initial token bias or beginning-of-sequence style/genre preference.

Plausible interpretation (not definitive)
- B appears to be more biased toward producing web/news/blog/clickbait/advert-like text compared to A. That could arise from a training-data or fine-tuning shift (more scraped blogs, news, ad-heavy webpages, or social-media text in B), but the evidence does not uniquely identify the training objective or the precise cause.

Uncertainties / caveats
- I cannot say exactly why the shift exists (e.g., which dataset or fine-tune) from this evidence alone.
- Patchscope continuations were not shown here, so I am relying mainly on the logit-lens tokens and the layer/position norm pattern. If you want stronger confirmation, running the difference as a prompt patchscope and inspecting generated continuations (or measuring next-token probability changes on controlled prompts) would help.
